# Implementing MVC ToDo App with Ruby on Rails — Comprehensive Learning Guide ## Course Overview This course teaches you to build a fully-functional To-Do application using the **Model-View-Controller (MVC)** architectural pattern in **Ruby on Rails**. You'll learn how Rails organizes code into logical layers, manage application state, handle user interactions, and persist data to a database. **Who this course is for:** - Backend developers transitioning to or learning Rails - Full-stack developers who want structured web application patterns - Developers preparing for Rails-focused interviews or roles **Why it matters for interview prep:** - MVC is the dominant pattern in web development interviews - Rails is widely used in startups and established companies (Shopify, GitHub, Airbnb all use or used Rails) - Building a complete CRUD application demonstrates end-to-end capability - You'll learn testing, database design, and deployment concepts that appear in system design rounds --- ## Core Topics Covered - **Rails Fundamentals & Project Setup** — Understanding Rails conventions, file structure, and generators - **Models & Active Record** — Database design, validations, associations, and ORM patterns - **Controllers & Routing** — Request routing, action handling, RESTful conventions, and parameter passing - **Views & ERB Templating** — HTML generation, form helpers, partials, and view logic - **Database Migrations & Schema** — Creating tables, managing schema changes, and relationships - **CRUD Operations** — Creating, reading, updating, and deleting resources with Rails conventions - **Authentication & Authorization** — User sessions, password handling, and access control - **Testing with RSpec & Capybara** — Unit tests, integration tests, and test-driven development --- ## Learning Path Workflow ### Phase 1: Rails Fundamentals (Week 1–2) **Goal:** Understand Rails project structure and conventions. 1. Install Rails and create a new project 2. Explore the directory structure (app/, config/, db/, spec/) 3. Learn Rails naming conventions (models, controllers, views) 4. Understand the request-response cycle 5. Learn about Gemfile and dependencies **Checkpoint Task:** ```bash rails new todo_app cd todo_app rails generate model Task title:string description:text completed:boolean rails db:migrate ``` ### Phase 2: Models & Database Design (Week 2–3) **Goal:** Design and implement the Task model with validations and associations. 6. Create migrations and understand schema design 7. Write model validations 8. Add associations (User has_many Tasks) 9. Test models with RSpec 10. Implement model scopes and class methods **Checkpoint Task:** ```ruby # app/models/task.rb class Task < ApplicationRecord belongs_to :user validates :title, presence: true, length: { minimum: 3 } validates :description, length: { maximum: 1000 } scope :completed, -> { where(completed: true) } scope :pending, -> { where(completed: false) } scope :recent, -> { order(created_at: :desc) } end ``` ### Phase 3: Routing & Controllers (Week 3–4) **Goal:** Build RESTful controllers and understand Rails routing. 11. Define RESTful routes in config/routes.rb 12. Generate scaffold or build controllers manually 13. Implement CRUD actions (index, show, create, update, destroy) 14. Handle strong parameters 15. Implement flash messages and redirects **Checkpoint Task:** ```ruby # config/routes.rb Rails.application.routes.draw do resources :users do resources :tasks end end # app/controllers/tasks_controller.rb class TasksController < ApplicationController before_action :set_task, only: [:show, :edit, :update, :destroy] def index @user = User.find(params[:user_id]) @tasks = @user.tasks.recent end def create @task = Task.new(task_params) if @task.save redirect_to @task, notice: 'Task created.' else render :new end end private def task_params params.require(:task).permit(:title, :description, :completed) end end ``` ### Phase 4: Views & Form Helpers (Week 4–5) **Goal:** Create user interfaces with ERB templates and Rails form helpers. 16. Create view templates for list, show, new, edit actions 17. Use Rails form helpers (form_with, form_for) 18. Build partials for reusable components 19. Implement CSS framework integration (Bootstrap/Tailwind) 20. Add client-side validation feedback **Checkpoint Task:** ```erb

<%= @user.name %>'s Tasks

<%= link_to 'New Task', new_user_task_path(@user), class: 'btn btn-primary' %>
<% @tasks.each do |task| %> <%= render 'task_item', task: task %> <% end %>
<%= form_with(model: [@user, @task], local: true) do |form| %> <% if @task.errors.any? %>

<%= pluralize(@task.errors.count, "error") %>

    <% @task.errors.full_messages.each do |message| %>
  • <%= message %>
    • <% end %>
<% end %>
<%= form.label :title %> <%= form.text_field :title, required: true %>
<%= form.label :description %> <%= form.text_area :description, rows: 5 %>
<%= form.submit "Save Task" %>
<% end %> ``` ### Phase 5: User Authentication (Week 5–6) **Goal:** Implement user authentication and authorization. 21. Create User model with password handling (bcrypt) 22. Implement sessions and login/logout 23. Add authentication filters to controllers 24. Build authorization (user can only modify own tasks) 25. Handle edge cases (expired sessions, unauthorized access) **Checkpoint Task:** ```ruby # app/models/user.rb class User < ApplicationRecord has_secure_password has_many :tasks, dependent: :destroy validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true validates :password, length: { minimum: 8 } end # app/controllers/sessions_controller.rb class SessionsController < ApplicationController def create @user = User.find_by(email: params[:email]) if @user&.authenticate(params[:password]) session[:user_id] = @user.id redirect_to user_tasks_path(@user), notice: 'Logged in!' else render :new, alert: 'Invalid credentials' end end def destroy session[:user_id] = nil redirect_to root_path, notice: 'Logged out!' end end # app/controllers/application_controller.rb class ApplicationController < ActionController::Base before_action :authenticate_user! helper_method :current_user def current_user @current_user ||= User.find(session[:user_id]) if session[:user_id] end def authenticate_user! redirect_to login_path unless current_user end end ``` ### Phase 6: Testing with RSpec (Week 6–7) **Goal:** Write comprehensive tests for models, controllers, and integration. 26. Set up RSpec and factory_bot 27. Write model tests (validations, associations, scopes) 28. Write controller tests (actions, authorization) 29. Write integration tests with Capybara 30. Achieve >80% test coverage **Checkpoint Task:** ```ruby # spec/models/task_spec.rb require 'rails_helper' RSpec.describe Task
